metaDescription: Six corded electric dethatchers compared on amps, path width, depth settings and bag size, with notes on tines versus blades and when your lawn needs one.
expertTake: The WEN DT1516 with a 15 amp motor and a 20-blade scarifier head is the best all-round electric dethatcher, and the LawnMaster GVB1316 is the pick for a 16 inch path at 13 amps. The Sun Joe AJ801E is the light, cheap option for small lawns. If your thatch is under half an inch, you do not need any of them.
introParagraphs: Thatch is the layer of dead stems and roots that builds up between the green blades and the soil. A thin layer is healthy, but a thick one blocks water, air and fertilizer and shelters pests.

An electric dethatcher spins a reel of tines or blades just above the soil to pull that layer out. The right machine depends on how thick the thatch is, how big the lawn is and whether you want to rake only or also cut into the soil.

products.name: WEN DT1516 16 inch 15A 2-in-1 dethatcher and scarifier
products.description:
The DT1516 pairs a 15 amp motor turning the reel at up to 3,300 RPM with a 16 inch path, a five-position height control from plus one quarter to minus one half inch and a 20-blade scarifying head. A dethatching tine reel and the scarifier reel swap on one machine.

The tradeoff is that the maximum motor load comes with a short cord limit, since a 15 amp tool on a thin extension cord loses voltage and slows under thick thatch. Against the 13 amp WEN DT1315 it has two more amps and a wider path, which matters on dense turf. The five depth settings let you start shallow, which is the key to not scalping the lawn. In year three the usual wear items are the tine tips, the bag seams and the drive belt, all of which are cheap to replace. Because it draws close to the household limit, run it on its own outlet and avoid power strips.

Clear clippings from the reel after each session, check the belt and keep the bag zipper clean. Run the machine over a test strip and check the output: if you are bringing up green blades and soil, raise the setting. If the thatch stays put, drop it one notch. The machine is a fair weight to lift into a vehicle, so plan on an easy way to load it.
products.bestFor: Most lawns with moderate thatch that need a strong, adjustable machine.
cons: Bag fills quickly on thick thatch

products.name: LawnMaster GVB1316 16 inch 13A dethatcher and scarifier, 12 gal bag
products.description:
The GVB1316 uses a 13 amp motor reaching 3,700 RPM, a 16 inch path and a 12 gallon collection bag. It is a 2-in-1 that switches between dethatching and scarifying.

The tradeoff is power per inch: a 13 amp motor on a 16 inch reel has less headroom than the 15 amp WEN, so on heavy thatch it will slow and need slower walking. A higher RPM raises raking frequency, which helps on light thatch but does not make up for lower torque. Compared with the WEN it gives the same width at a lower amp rating.

Empty the bag often and keep the cord clear of the reel. The high reel speed makes more dust and debris, so wear eye protection and a dust mask, and rake up loose material afterward to finish the job.
products.bestFor: Larger lawns with light to moderate thatch.
cons: 13A has less headroom on a 16 inch reel

products.name: BILT HARD 16 inch 15A dethatcher scarifier, 5 depth positions
products.description:
The BILT HARD has a 15 amp copper motor up to 3,300 RPM, a 16 inch path, five depth positions and both a dethatching roller and a scarifying roller.

The tradeoff is brand maturity. The spec sheet nearly matches the WEN DT1516, so you are choosing between a known name and a value brand, and parts supply for the newer name is less certain. Copper windings are standard in a motor of this class, so treat them as a basic feature.

Keep a spare roller in mind and check the quick-release latch regularly. Because both rollers ride on the same shaft, a bent roller shows up as vibration through the handle, and a wobbling reel tears turf unevenly. After the first hour of use, check that the reel bolts are tight.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want 15A power at a value price.

products.name: MZK 15 inch 13A electric dethatcher scarifier, 12 gal bag
products.description:
The MZK offers a 13 amp copper motor at 3,700 RPM, a 15 inch rake path, adjustable depth from minus 0.47 to plus 0.24 inch and a 12 gallon bag.

The tradeoff is that it is a lesser-known brand with specs similar to the LawnMaster, so the choice comes down to price and availability. Its depth range is broader on the scarifying side than most, which suits renovation work.

Store it dry and clear the reel after use. Its bag is a standard 12 gallon size, so replacement bags from similar models are easy to find. On a big job, expect to empty it every few minutes in thick thatch. Work in straight overlapping lines like mowing, and cross-hatch a second pass at right angles only if the first left thatch behind.
products.bestFor: Renovation work on mid-size lawns at a lower price.

products.name: Sun Joe AJ801E 12A dethatcher scarifier, 12.6 inch, 8 gal bag
products.description:
The AJ801E has a 12 amp motor, a 12.6 inch path, five depth positions and an 8 gallon bag. It is the smallest machine here and is sold by a brand with a long record of parts support.

The tradeoff is width and bag size: 12.6 inches means more passes and an 8 gallon bag fills sooner. On a lawn of 2,000 square feet that is still a morning's work, and the machine is gentle enough for a first-time user. It is a good fit for a small yard where the light weight and easy storage matter more than speed. Compared with the 16 inch machines it is lighter to carry and cheaper to run.

Wipe the reel and check the cord before each use. A cord clip near the handle keeps the cord out of the path, and working away from the outlet means the cord always trails behind the machine. The light body suits older gardeners or anyone who finds a 30 pound machine hard to turn.
products.bestFor: Small yards where weight and storage matter.

products.name: Greenworks 13A 14 inch corded dethatcher scarifier, 3 positions
products.description:
The Greenworks uses a 13 amp motor, a 14 inch path, three depth positions and a quick-release system for swapping reels, with a push-button start.

The tradeoff is the three-position depth control, which is coarser than the five-position settings on rivals. A coarse depth range increases the scalping risk on uneven lawns. Its strength is a light, easy-to-handle body and fast reel changes.

Keep the reel clear and store the machine dry. Swap reels with the power unplugged and the reel stopped. Because the depth lever has only three notches, test on a hidden corner of the lawn first and adjust one notch at a time.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Tines are flexible spring steel that comb out surface thatch, while blades cut into the soil and also open the turf for seed. Most machines here are 2-in-1 with both reels, such as the WEN DT1516 with 20 blades. A tine-only machine lifts moss but leaves it on the lawn.

A 15 amp motor like the WEN or BILT HARD has the headroom for thick thatch, whereas a 12 amp Sun Joe suits light work. Use a 14 gauge or heavier outdoor extension cord, since a thin cord causes voltage drop and stalling. Keep the run to 50 feet or less and plug into a GFCI outlet.

Five positions, as on the WEN and Sun Joe, let you start shallow and step down. The Greenworks has only three. A fixed or coarse depth risks scalping on uneven ground. Begin at the shallowest setting. A healthy lawn recovers from a light pass in two weeks, but one aggressive pass can set it back for a season.

A 16 inch path covers more ground than a 12.6 inch one, which can cut a large lawn's job by a quarter. The tradeoff is weight and turning room, so measure gates and beds before buying a wide machine. Bags run from 8 gallons on the Sun Joe to 12 gallons on the LawnMaster and MZK, and fill fast on thick thatch. A full bag is also heavy and bulky, so a smaller bag you empty often can be easier on the back than a large one.

Check thatch with a spade cut: under half an inch is healthy. Dethatch when the lawn is actively growing, early fall for cool-season grass, and when the soil is moist but not soaked. Avoid dethatching during drought, heat or dormancy, because the turf cannot recover and weeds move in. Water the lawn a day before if the ground is dry. Mow short first. Set the mower one notch lower than usual, bag the clippings, and rake loose debris before the machine goes in so the reel is not clogged by long grass.

These machines weigh 20 to 35 pounds and are awkward to lift into a car. Dethatchers also leave a lot of debris, so plan for a tarp and a compost bin for the clippings. Check where it will live and how you will move it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor and reel
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared amps from 12 to 15 and reel speeds from 3,300 to 3,700 RPM, weighing amps more for thick thatch. High reel speed with low torque was not treated as an advantage.

howWeEvaluated.title: Depth control
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared three-position and five-position systems and the range each covers. Coarse systems were marked down because they make it harder to avoid scalping.

howWeEvaluated.title: Width and bag
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared widths from 12.6 to 16 inches and bags from 8 to 12 gallons.

howWeEvaluated.title: Reel versatility
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at tine and blade reels and quick-release designs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on the spec sheet and owner feedback patterns, we weighed cord needs, brand support and tine wear.

cards.label: Tines
cards.text: Spring tines comb thatch out of turf gently. Use them for light to moderate thatch.

cards.label: Blades
cards.text: Blades cut into soil and open the turf for seed. Use them for renovation and heavy buildup.

howToChoose.note: Tines for maintenance. Blades for renovation.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a blade reel and a wide depth range. Seed needs bare soil contact, so pass the blades in two directions, rake off the debris and sow seed straight away. Keep the new seed damp for two to three weeks.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The WEN DT1516 with 20 blades and the MZK with a wide depth range fit best.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if your thatch is thick or your lawn is large. The WEN DT1516 justifies it, because extra amps mean fewer stalls and a shorter job.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if you dethatch once a year on a small lawn. The Sun Joe is enough, and the savings can go toward seed and fertilizer.

maintenance.why: Clippings wrap and add load, and a packed reel slows the motor and tears turf. Flip the machine on its side with the plug out, and clear it with a stick or a brush, never your fingers.
Worn tines lift less thatch and leave a patchy result. Replace a full set rather than one tine, so the reel stays balanced.
Damaged insulation is a shock hazard.
A slipping belt loses power and squeals on startup. Check its tension and look for glazing or cracks, and replace it before it breaks mid-job.
Moisture rusts carbon steel, so wipe the tines with an oily rag and hang the machine off the floor.

faq.q: How do I know I need to dethatch?
faq.a: Cut a plug with a spade. If the thatch is thicker than half an inch, dethatch. Thinner than that, the layer feeds the soil and a rake once a year is plenty.
When the lawn is actively growing: early fall for cool-season grass, late spring for warm-season. Avoid dormant, drought-stressed or newly seeded lawns.
Tines for maintenance, blades for renovation. Many gardeners use the tine reel in spring and the blade reel once every year or two in early fall.
A 14 gauge or heavier outdoor cord.
Not if you start at the shallowest setting. Too deep tears healthy roots, and a lawn that looks rough for a week is normal while it recovers.
Yes, after a blade pass, since seed contacts soil. Spread seed at the rate on the bag, rake lightly and water daily until it sprouts.
